targets.query:
from(bucket: "firewalls")
  |> range(start: -24h)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "pan_system" and r.hostname == "${hostname}" and r._field == "uptime")
  |> group()
  |> last()
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ _time: r._time, _field: "Uptime", _value: float(v: r._value) / 8640000.0 }))

from(bucket: "firewalls")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "pan_hr_processors" and r.hostname == "${hostname}" and r._field == "processor_load_pct")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ r with _field: if r.device_index == "1" then "MP" else if r.device_index == "2" then "DP" else "CPU " + string(v: r.device_index) }))
  |> group(columns: ["_field"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: mean, createEmpty: false)
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> drop(columns: ["_start", "_stop"])

panels.title: CPU MP / DP
panels.description: Processor load exposed by Palo Alto HOST-RESOURCES SNMP table. On small appliances this usually maps to Management Plane and Data Plane; larger platforms may expose more processor entries.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "firewalls")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "pan_system" and r.hostname == "${hostname}" and r._field =~ /^ram_(total|used)_kb$/)
  |> pivot(rowKey:["_time"], columnKey:["_field"], valueColumn:"_value")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => exists r.ram_total_kb and exists r.ram_used_kb and r.ram_total_kb > 0)
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ _time: r._time, _field: "RAM", _value: float(v: r.ram_used_kb) / float(v: r.ram_total_kb) * 100.0 }))
  |> group(columns: ["_field"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: mean, createEmpty: false)
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> drop(columns: ["_start", "_stop"])

panels.title: Memory and Packet Buffer Usage
panels.description: Dataplane packet buffer and descriptor pools from HOST-RESOURCES hrStorageTable. Management-plane memory is intentionally excluded here.

targets.query:
from(bucket: "firewalls")
  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._measurement == "pan_hr_storage" and r.hostname == "${hostname}")
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r._field == "storage_usage_pct" or r._field == "storage_size" or r._field == "storage_used" or r._field == "allocation_units")
  |> last()
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["storage_index", "storage_descr"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({ r with
    storage_type: if r.storage_descr =~ /(?i)(packet descriptors|on-chip|descriptor)/ then "Dataplane descriptors" else if r.storage_descr =~ /(?i)(hardware packet buffers|packet buffers|packet buffer)/ then "Dataplane packet buffers" else if r.storage_descr =~ /(?i)(management memory|memory)/ then "Management memory" else if r.storage_descr =~ /(?i)(disk|filesystem|tmp|var|opt|root|boot|log)/ then "Filesystem / disk" else "Other hrStorage pool",
    used_pct: if exists r.storage_usage_pct then float(v: r.storage_usage_pct) else if exists r.storage_used and exists r.storage_size and r.storage_size > 0 then float(v: r.storage_used) / float(v: r.storage_size) * 100.0 else 0.0,
    size_bytes: if exists r.storage_size and exists r.allocation_units then float(v: r.storage_size) * float(v: r.allocation_units) else 0.0,
    used_bytes: if exists r.storage_used and exists r.allocation_units then float(v: r.storage_used) * float(v: r.allocation_units) else 0.0
  }))
  |> keep(columns: ["storage_type", "storage_descr", "used_pct", "used_bytes", "size_bytes", "storage_used", "storage_size", "allocation_units", "storage_index"])
  |> sort(columns: ["storage_type", "storage_descr"])

panels.title: Storage Pool Details
panels.description: Raw HOST-RESOURCES-MIB hrStorageTable entries exposed by PAN-OS. This is not only disk: Palo Alto also reports management memory, dataplane packet buffers, and descriptor pools here. Used/Size are shown both as bytes when allocation_units is meaningful and as raw hrStorage units for troubleshooting.
